sources.title: Plectic Heegner classes
selectors: §1.1.1 Relation to mock plectic invariants, Theorem B
claims: For an incoherent set S, epsilon(A/E)=(-1)^(|S|+1).
When F=Q, an incoherent set contains at most one prime.
For F=Q, S=empty gives a linear combination of Kummer images of classical Heegner points.
For F=Q, S={p}, the comparison to mock plectic invariants is Theorem B, and the local sign epsilon_p is defined according to split/non-split multiplicative reduction of A/Q_p.
The higher-rank Selmer/arithmetic significance of the plectic Heegner classes in §1.2 is stated conjecturally.

sources.title: Iwasawa theory and mock plectic points
claims: The mock-plectic Iwasawa setup uses p inert in an imaginary quadratic field K.
The elliptic curve E/Q is assumed to have multiplicative reduction at p.
Nonvanishing of Q_K is an input implying p-Selmer rank two under the stated hypotheses; it is not derived there from analytic rank two.

sources.title: Nonvanishing of generalised Kato classes and Iwasawa main conjectures
claims: Generalised Kato classes are available for positive even analytic rank at primes p>3 of good ordinary reduction.
The proved implication is kappa_p(E) nonzero => Q_p-Selmer dimension two; the converse is conditional on a nonzero localization map.
This is a candidate representation rotation, not a proof that analytic rank two forces nonzero kappa_p(E).

premises: R5 preserves exact complex order two after base change whenever the complementary quadratic twist has nonzero central value.
Exact order two has functional-equation sign +1.
derivation: With F=Q and |S|<=1, the even-sign branch forces S={p}; S=empty is the sign -1/classical-Heegner branch.
The S={p} comparison to mock plectic invariants is formulated with A/Q_p of split or non-split multiplicative reduction, and Fornea–Gehrmann explicitly assumes multiplicative reduction at p.
Therefore the audited F=Q even-sign mock-plectic route has an E-intrinsic multiplicative-reduction entry condition before auxiliary K-selection.
not_claimed: No claim that every plectic construction or every future plectic method requires multiplicative reduction.
No claim that an arbitrary elliptic curve lacks a multiplicative prime.
No claim that the BSD root hypothesis supplies the required interface.
No inference from construction/nonvanishing conjectures to BSD.

falsifiers_checked: F=Q S=empty supplies the same even-sign rank-two carrier: REJECTED_BY_SIGN_AND_SOURCE_ROLE

F=Q S={p} admits good/additive reduction in the audited mock-plectic comparison: NOT_SUPPORTED; source defines split/non-split multiplicative cases and the Iwasawa paper explicitly requires multiplicative reduction
multiplicative-reduction wording is merely expository: REJECTED for the audited Fornea–Gehrmann theorem by the abstract/setup
auxiliary K changes reduction type of fixed E/Q: REJECTED as a typing error; K changes splitting/inertness, not E's intrinsic local reduction type
